text:
nora: flagging a slow creep since 02:05 UTC in us-west2: tiny-pod attach storms leading to 0.25/0.5 GPU slots scattered across racks. pending-tiny-pods climbed from 90 -> 410 in 45m, and attach failures are up. apps seeing degraded tail latency.

tay: any node logs? i want to check attach/fail loops and conntrack.

nora: pasted one from node usw2-nv-07 at 02:12:
```
Feb 21 02:12:10 kubelet[2987]: attach: claim failed: device busy
Feb 21 02:12:11 kubelet[2987]: attach: timeout waiting for disk/attach, context deadline exceeded
Feb 21 02:12:11 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
Feb 21 02:12:12 kubelet[2987]: evicting pod tiny-runner-5f2 due to attach timeout
```

rafael: interesting: the scheduler is still preferring spread across NVLink groups for anti-affinity policy; small pods end up scattered. that increases attach ops and cross-rack traffic when we warm nodes.

meera: infra-bot alert: us-west2: attach-failure-rate > threshold (alert_id: infra:attach:3567).

ops-lead: we need immediate throttle + packing change. quick options: 1) soft-prebind tiny-pods onto nodes with existing tiny-pods (coalesce), 2) add per-node attach-rate limiter in warm-pool controller, 3) bump nf_conntrack_max on a tiny canary group.

tay: i prefer rate-limiter + scheduler hint as first line. bumping conntrack is risky across the fleet. rate-limiter can be applied at controller-side without kernel changes.

rafael: i'll ship a scheduler patch that adds a PriorityScore for tiny-pod coalescing: prefer nodes where tiny_count > 0, algorithm: score += 100 * min(1, tiny_count/4), and tie-break on GPU free capacity. PR: https://github.com/redwood/scheduler/pull/4217 (wip).

nora: thanks. i've also seen many attach retries with websocket errors and intermittent TLS close 1006 between kubelet and attach service. seems like connection churn + conntrack exhaustion.

meera: doing a canary: plan proposed:
- deploy attach-rate-limiter to warm-pool-controller in us-west2-a (limit=8 attaches/sec)
- enable scheduler coalesce on 8 canary nodes (label canary=tinypack)
- monitor for 20m: metrics attach-p95, evict-rate, pending-tiny-pods, node-conntrack.
SLA: evict-rate < 5/min and attach-p95 < 25s within 20m or rollback.

ops-lead: include rollback steps: remove label + restore controller env var and redeploy. Tag canary nodes in infra console.

tay: also propose making warm-pool attach jitter: random backoff between 50-250ms per attach attempt to spread conn usage. low-risk change.

rafael: added a small QOL: scheduler coalesce respects tenant placement constraints (do not violate tenant affinity/anti-affinity). We'll expose a toggle cluster-wide first.

nora: canary started at 02:30 UTC. initial numbers after 6m: pending-tiny-pods -28%, evictions -33%, attach-p95 down from 38s to 19s. will continue to watch.

meera: watchlist: node mem/cpu (coalescing increases CPU density), nf_conntrack_count, kubelet attach queue lengths. if nf_conntrack grows > 75% of max on canary nodes, abort.

ops-lead: post-canary follow ups: 1) add telemetry: count of attach ops avoided by coalescing per-tenant, 2) evaluate enabling per-node conntrack bump only for warm node family, 3) consider long-term: server-side attach multiplexing or persistent device proxies to avoid socket churn.

infra-bot: [update] canary metrics at 02:38: attach-p95=18.9s, evict-rate=4.2/min, pending-tiny-pods=290 (was 405).

nora: noting cost tradeoff: coalescing fewer nodes increases CPU/host contention but avoids launching extra warm instances and large egress. cost delta is likely lower.

meera: proceeding with 30m observation window. i'll post a final summary at 03:00 UTC and either schedule rollout or rollback.

rafael: if rollout succeeds let's make the scheduler hint opt-in per-namespace (feature flag) so tenants can decide density vs spread.

nora: thanks all. will update incident doc and link PRs. rolling watch. :eyes:
